Gemini 1.5 Flash 420ms 742 tokens

To integrate Google Gemini into Next.js 14 App Router securely, invoke the Google Generative AI SDK inside a server-side Route Handler (app/api/chat/route.ts). This ensures your GEMINI_API_KEY is never leaked to the client browser.

security
Security Practice: Always configure environment variables in .env.local without the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix to prevent bundling into client scripts.
javascript app/api/chat/route.ts 
import { GoogleGenerativeAI } from '@google/generative-ai';
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';

// Initialize the Google Gemini client server-side
const genAI = new GoogleGenerativeAI(process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY || '');

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  try {
    const { prompt, model = 'gemini-1.5-flash' } = await req.json();

    if (!prompt) {
      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Prompt is required' }, { status: 400 });
    }

    const generativeModel = genAI.getGenerativeModel({ model });
    const result = await generativeModel.generateContent(prompt);
    const response = await result.response;

    return NextResponse.json({
      text: response.text(),
      model,
      usage: response.usageMetadata
    });
  } catch (error: any) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: error.message }, { status: 500 });
  }
}

Next Step: You can consume this endpoint directly from your React Server or Client Components using standard fetch('/api/chat', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ prompt }) }).

For token streaming, leverage generateContentStream() combined with Next.js web standard ReadableStream:

  • Convert Gemini's asynchronous iterable chunk into a TextEncoder().encode(chunk.text()) byte stream.
  • Return an instance of new Response(stream, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8' } }).
  • In client components, consume using the browser's native response.body.getReader() for smooth UI typing.

Next.js 14 + Gemini Project Architecture

Configuration, environment variables, and route handler implementation

Recommended Next.js App Router tree isolating AI generation logic:

my-gemini-nextjs-app/
├── app/
│   ├── api/
│   │   └── chat/
│   │       └── route.ts          # Server-side Gemini API route handler
│   ├── layout.tsx                # App Root layout
│   └── page.tsx                  # Client chat user interface
├── components/
│   ├── ChatInterface.tsx         # Conversation renderer
│   ├── MessageItem.tsx           # Rich Markdown & Code container
│   └── PromptInput.tsx           # Auto-expanding composer
├── lib/
│   └── gemini.ts                 # GoogleGenerativeAI client singleton
├── .env.local                    # Secret API Key (Never commit to Git!)
└── package.json

Create a .env.local file in your project root with your Google AI Studio credentials:

# Obtain key from https://aistudio.google.com/
GEMINI_API_KEY=AIzaSyD-YourOfficialKeyGoesHere

# Optional Runtime config
GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-1.5-flash
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
⚠️ Note: Do not prefix GEMINI_API_KEY with NEXT_PUBLIC_. The key must only be accessible by Node/Edge environments.

Complete implementation for app/api/chat/route.ts:

import { GoogleGenerativeAI } from '@google/generative-ai';
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';

const apiKey = process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error('Missing GEMINI_API_KEY');

const genAI = new GoogleGenerativeAI(apiKey);

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const { message } = await req.json();
  const model = genAI.getGenerativeModel({ model: 'gemini-1.5-flash' });
  
  const response = await model.generateContent(message);
  return NextResponse.json({ text: response.response.text() });
}

Install official Google Generative AI SDK and development dependencies:

# 1. Install Google Generative AI SDK
npm install @google/generative-ai

# 2. Run local development server
npm run dev
